chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim said, and the trustworthy one (1) from the Ahl al-Bayt narrated to us from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) that he said:

"Intend the Tamattu' Hajj with the Talbiyah from the Day of Tarwiyah until the decline of the sun, and after Asr, and after Maghrib, and after 'Isha; the time between all of these is broad (permissible)."
As for what has been narrated regarding the missing of that (time), it has been narrated.

key_terms.الْمُتْعَةِ بِالْحَجِّ: Tamattu' Hajj (a type of pilgrimage where Umrah and Hajj are performed separately)
key_terms.زَوَالِ الشَّمْسِ: Decline of the sun (Zawal, time for Dhuhr prayer)
key_terms.يَوْمَ التَّرْوِيَةِ: The Day of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: When can a pilgrim enter Ihram for Tamattu' Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the temporal flexibility for entering Ihram for Tamattu' Hajj, extending the window from the Day of Tarwiyah through the night until sunset. By explicitly including periods after Asr, Maghrib, and 'Isha, the Imam emphasizes that the validity is not restricted to daylight hours, providing practical ease for pilgrims. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the precise start of the Hajj ritual state.
